The method contains two distinct Arrange-Act-Assert scenarios: one for N=473 and an additional small-boundary check for a single vertex. This is multiple 'Act' operations in one test, violating atomicity.
The test uses only local variables (N, grafo0, single) and does not rely on shared mutable state or numbered test names. No setup/teardown is required for this single test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only this single test method and only exercises happy-path behavior. There are no tests for error conditions or exceptional inputs (no assertThrows/@Test(expected=...), and total test count is <2).
The test explicitly includes a small-boundary check for a single-vertex graph (createGraph(1) and assertEquals(1)), covering a boundary case.
No helper methods or constants are introduced for repeated setup; the test duplicates graph creation logic within the same method. There is no extracted common setup utility in this class.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is short (simple linear flow, no loops or conditionals) and under typical length thresholds; cyclomatic complexity is low.
The test contains two assertions (one for the large graph and one for the single-vertex boundary), avoiding the single-superficial-assert anti-pattern; assertions are specific (assertEquals).
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out test methods are present; tests are active and runnable.
The class Javadoc includes explicit requirement traceability lines (REQ-GRAPH-001 .. REQ-GRAPH-004), linking tests to requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test of basic graph behavior; there are no explicit performance or security tests expected here and no timing/security assertions are present.
The test method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome, violating recommended naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The class uses EvoSuite/EvoRunner and the test method has an auto-generated style name ('test7'), suggesting the test was generated. This indicates heavy test-generation artifacts rather than minimal hand-written tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level Javadoc describes Given-When-Then structure and requirement mapping, indicating thoughtful test design and prioritization.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API (createGraph, numVertices) and does not access private fields or use reflection; it focuses on observable behavior.
Assertions use specific assertEquals with descriptive messages rather than generic assertTrue; messages aid diagnosis.
The test includes succinct Given-When-Then comments and the class has useful Javadoc; there are no commented-out code blocks.
The test uses fixed inputs and no sources of non-determinism (no Random(), time calls, or Thread.sleep()). EvoRunner parameters do not introduce nondeterminism in the visible method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses local graphs and does not persist files, modify static state, or leave resources open; no cleanup is required.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing a meaningful classification for selective execution.

PRINCIPLE: A test should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single Arrange-Act-Assert aids root-cause identification. EVALUATION: The method performs an insertion (insereAresta) and then computes grafoTransposto() and asserts both insertion and transpose properties — multiple distinct operations. DECISION: More than one distinct action related to behavior (insertion + transpose) present -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test exercises multiple operations in one method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent. EVALUATION: Method uses only local variables (N, v, grafo0, grafo1) and does not rely on shared mutable state or ordering annotations. DECISION: No @Before/@After required and no shared mutable state observed. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover happy path and error scenarios. EVALUATION: The class contains a single test method exercising a happy path; no tests for invalid inputs or exceptions (no assertThrows or @Test(expected=...)). DECISION: Only happy-path coverage present -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should include boundary and edge values. EVALUATION: Test uses N=473 and v=1 (typical values); no zero, negative, max index, or empty graph cases are tested. DECISION: No boundary inputs present -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be modular and avoid duplication. EVALUATION: The method is short, uses createGraph() helper (from scaffolding) and follows Arrange-Act-Assert comments. DECISION: No duplicated blocks in this single-test class and test is concise -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should be small and simple. EVALUATION: Method is linear, contains no loops or conditionals, and is well under complexity thresholds. DECISION: Meets size and complexity criteria -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties. EVALUATION: The test checks multiple properties (instance identity, vertex count, and edge existence in original and transpose) — multiple assertions verifying different aspects. DECISION: Multi-property verification present -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be active and not ignored. EVALUATION: No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out tests in the provided snippet. DECISION: All tests are active -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should link to requirements. EVALUATION: Class Javadoc includes explicit requirement IDs (REQ-GRAPH-001 .. REQ-GRAPH-004). DECISION: Traceability present in class comments -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.
